columns.header: When decided: before or after seeing what it produced (what had been seen)

value.format: common to the series, assumed relief depth D = {D_mm} mm

reason.why: keeps the depth differences between sentences

value.literal: four shown together, the series using the grey of the height; grey; lit at 45 degrees from upper left, lower right; stretched per tile

reason.why: also a quantity the maker sets (one viewpoint)

rows_work1.when: after: every image and value of work 1

value.text: MEmoLon (Japanese) through map B, fitted to English ratings

reason.why: brings the Japanese values onto the English scale
later_compared: two other maps, on check sentences

judged.text: two makers (one blind), with the sheet and example

value.text: V and A as percentiles in the 23 works, each author weighted equally

reason.why: undoes the compression of map B (drops distances between values)

rows_work2.when: after: the whole-lexicon percentiles and the sketches

row_rule: the main text shows only the rows that bear on its claims (decision of the researcher, 2026-10-29, on the word count): the two sides of each comparison whose effect the paper reports (work 1: the height scale, whose alternative is the per-tile min-max, and the drawing; work 2: map B and the percentiles); the subject of work 2, a decision about what the paper claims and not a quantity of the works, and every other decision of works 1 and 2 are in the full table of supplement S1, with the longer wording (decision 1 of the researcher after round 8)
acted_on_labels: in the repository the column holds the image files; the numbers of the figures of the paper are put in when the manuscript is made, outside the repository

layout.empty_template: the same table with the six headers and three empty rows is drawn below it
layout.row_order: a band 'Work 1' and its rows, then a band 'Work 2' and its rows, each in the order of the conditions
layout.reason_format: '{why}. Tried: {a}; {b}.' or '{why}. Tried: none.', followed by ' Later compared with: {c}; {d}.' when later_compared is not empty and by ' Not tried: {e}; {f}.' when not_tried is not empty, with the first letter of why in upper case
layout.print: drawn in one grey channel (mode L) on white, with no colour; every font size is at least 7 pt at the printed width
layout.note: under the filled table, one line: the text of note

outputs: results/decision_note_v7/decision_note.png, decision_note.md (the same table as text) and decision_note.json (the values read, the SHA-256 of the conditions, the counts of words); results/decision_note (version 2), results/decision_note_v4, results/decision_note_v5 and results/decision_note_v6 are kept
words: the words drawn are counted as whitespace-separated tokens of the text of each cell (as built by the script), the headers, the band labels, the note and the titles, for the filled and the empty table; a path of an image is one word and a mark standing alone (*) is also one word; the counts are recorded and enter the word count of the outline (the template of the journal counts tables and charts); the run stops if the two tables together exceed max_words
not_claimed: A way of noting decisions; it does not show that noting them helps a reader (no study with people). Disclosure helps a reader repeat the work but does not by itself settle whether a reading is valid or a choice biased. The column of who judged names the judgement made, not the viewers of the paper; 'none recorded' means no look was judged with a sheet, not that the makers did not look. The four rows are chosen by the rule above, not as the decisions that mattered most. The reasons are the makers' statements as recorded in the decision table; they are not checked against a file and do not show that a choice was right. The judged cells of work 2 speak of the row of the 20 words only (the other rows of the blind judgement are in S1); they were judged on the images of the judgement (80 px tiles under five common seeds), not on figure 6 itself. The share used is a record of the 40 words of two trial authors, chosen as the authors of the largest and the smallest fluctuation of V (the standard deviation of the means of windows of 40 sentences, averaged over each author's works; check 4 of the overall inspection), after it was seen, not a property of the map or of the lexicon (the shares on the reference sets are in S1); the minimum to maximum is sensitive to one extreme word and the quartiles are in S1; using more of a range is not claimed to be better. 'Later compared with' names an alternative computed after the decision was set; it is not a reason of the decision.
checks: every file named exists and is the one at HEAD; every key read exists; every must_contain string occurs in the keys named (else the run stops)
every image of compared is one of acted_on of its row; the judged of each row is 'none recorded', a literal checked where a check is given, or a text with answers; no row carries the dagger
every row has a reason with a non-empty why and lists tried, later_compared and not_tried of non-empty strings (possibly empty)
2 rows of work 1 and 2 of work 2 (asserted as constants), and 6 columns
the saved image, opened again, is mode L at the width of the layout and its dpi, the font drawn (after rounding to pixels) is at least 7 pt, and the note is one line
the words of the two tables together are at most max_words
the share used of each quantity named in used_range is computed by used_range_rule, its rounding is the string shown for that quantity, and the phrase of the share is built from it
the outcome of every judged row with answers is computed by answers_rule from the two lists, is the outcome written, and the phrase of the outcome is built from it

no text of a row (quantity, value, reason, image paths, when, judged) contains a reserved mark, and no literal contains a percentage or, in a row of work 2, names words (reserved_marks, required_checks)
the ids of the rows are, in order, those fixed in the script (w1_height_scale, w1_drawing; w2_map_b, w2_percentiles); the version of each row of work 2 is read by its id
every cell of every row, before a phrase is built and with its kind, equals the cell fixed in the script for that row id (approved_text_rule)
the files of the two judges are the ones fixed in the script (main: results/blind_judgement/score.json, also: results/blind_judgement/score-researcher-supplement.json) and differ

no cell holds a percentage, a percent sign (also full-width) or the word percent or per cent, except the value of a row with used_range, whose percentages are exactly the two built from the record, in the order f, s; this holds for every kind of value, a format of keys included
for each version and quantity of used_range, the smallest and the largest of pooled equal the smallest and the largest of the 40 words listed under that version
the words listed under each version in the record number, author by author, as words_per_author

dagger.meaning: claim weakened in the paper after the values were seen

used_range_rule: the range of a quantity is the one the rule can give, read from atact.mapping (f in [F0, F0 + F1], s in [S0, S0 + S1], the ends of p and q in [0, 1]); its share used is (the largest minus the smallest value of the 40 words of the two trial authors, pooled, the key pooled.<version>.<quantity> of the record) divided by that range, in percent, rounded to a whole number ('N%'), which must equal shown.<quantity>; the quantities must be exactly f and s, and the words per author of the record must sum to words. The value is built as '{text}; f and s of the {words} words use {f} and {s} of their ranges (min to max; counted later, from the record)', the phrase fixed in the script. The smallest to the largest is sensitive to an outlier; the quartiles are in S1
answers_rule: the judged of a row of work 2 covers one version and one row of the blind judgement: the row remains for a judge if it is in the list of that version (main: the deciding judge of score.json, called the main judge in the paper, whose decided must be true; also: the researcher, of the supplement, whose controls must pass); the outcome is 'both differ' if both lists hold the row, 'neither' if none does and 'split' otherwise; the run stops unless the outcome is the one written. The judged is built as '{text}; for {phrase of the row} {phrase of the outcome}', with the phrases fixed in the script ('both differ': 'both said the rows differ', 'split': 'they split', 'neither': 'neither said the rows differ'; 'words20': 'the 20 words'; a row without a phrase stops the run); the row must be one of the rows of works/conditions/blind_judgement.json, and the version of the answers must be the version of the used_range of the same row. The other rows and versions are in S1
reserved_marks: the dagger and the mark of the compared images are drawn only by the script: a row whose quantity, value, reason, image paths, when or judged contains † or * stops the run
required_checks: a percentage may appear in a value only through used_range, and an outcome of the judgement only through answers: a literal that contains a percentage, or a literal judged of a row of work 2 that names words, stops the run
note: Judged: whether the two authors' rows differ within one version; versions not compared.
approved_text_rule: every cell of the four rows as written in these conditions (the quantity, the value before a phrase is built with its kind: format, literal or text, the reason as built from its parts, the time, and the judged before a phrase is built with its kind, or 'none recorded') is fixed per row id in the script, character for character, so that changing any of them needs a change of the script as well as of these conditions; the check of reserved words (SAID) stays as a second check
